failures.criterion: A8, 'each changed statement's time is lower after', for relatedProbeSQL, and the committed harness that holds it.
failures.evidence: The pair this round added (64e137bb, 'the related-terms probe's A8 reading is a pair on one database') is a coin flip on the measurement database, and three of my four runs are red: 'relatedProbeSQL: the after text's median is 3.992ms, not below the before text's 3.99ms', then 4.721ms against 4.672ms, then 4.521ms against 4.498ms, with one run green at 4.437ms against 4.46ms. The two texts cost the same at this size, within half a per cent either way, and the after plan reaches document_search through its primary key (Index Scan using document_search_pkey, 4 loops of 0.75 rows), not through the GIN index, because the probe looks each candidate document up by id rather than searching the table. So the committed test is flaky as written, and A8's 'lower after' is not supportable for this statement on this fixture. Two ways out, the architect's to choose: make it a head-side reading with its plan and the reason, as the five document-arm statements are, or give the pair a subject at which the index decides - the implementer's own trickyParts say the index wins on its own merits at two thousand documents, and this fixture holds forty thousand of which the probe touches four.

notes: The census, A9 and the before side were not re-measured this round. The head conflicts with main, so it will move before anything can merge, and the two failures above decide the round on their own; those three were re-taken by the implementer on a database of its own this round, and this phase re-takes them at the head that answers CI.

The measurement Postgres of this round is the implementer's durable Job, infra-325-durable-5bsbp in the builds namespace, holding the main-schema copy and the head-schema copy of one seed. It must be deleted when the last measurement is done: kubectl -n builds delete job infra-325-durable-5bsbp, which takes its Service with it. My own earlier Job, infra-325-postgres-wb4f6, is already gone.

A note for whoever reads the probe failure: the probe's after plan is not wrong. It reaches document_search by primary key because the statement looks four candidate documents up by id, which is the cheapest thing a plan can do; the GIN index has nothing to decide there. What the pair claims - that the after text is faster - is what the fixture cannot show.
